page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.25 GHz, allocating 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This architecture establishes a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core), deliberately prioritizing raw compute capacity over expansive memory footprints.

The hardware configuration includes 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without bundled local disks, relying entirely on remote cloud storage options. Additionally, no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. Because hardware resources focus heavily on processor cycles without the overhead of surplus RAM or unneeded local storage controllers, resource density remains high for pure computational tasks.

The trade-off of this resource allocation lies in its constrained memory-to-core ratio and absence of local scratch disks, making it suboptimal for memory-intensive caching layers or large in-memory datasets. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.2xlarge is structurally configured for compute-bound workloads, such as distributed compilation, batch processing, continuous integration pipelines, and CPU-driven web application serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AMD EPYC 9T95 processor on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 2.25 GHz and 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local storage and contains zero GPUs, operating strictly with remote storage architectures. By dedicating its hardware balance toward CPU capacity rather than memory excess, it delivers high compute density relative to its resource profile. The ecs.c9ae.2xlarge is primarily engineered for compute-heavy workloads that operate within lean memory boundaries, including continuous integration and deployment pipelines, distributed processing jobs, code compilation, and scalable stateless application serving.
